newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds closed off their peak on Thursday after rising strongly in mid-afternoon on remarks from the Bundesbank, which boosted bund futures.

The Bundesbank said earlier it expected German inflation to remain below two percent for the next two years and Bundesbank council member Hans-Juergen Krupp said the German central bank could not ignore record German jobless figures issued last week.
"This means there are still good buying opportunities as soon as prices edge only a little lower," said one dealer.
Most business was in the 2001-2006 area.
Dealers said the market was somewhat short of the Benchmark 2006 guilder-bond.
Dealers were divided on tomorrow's new tap issue, some opted for a reopening of the September 2002, while others were expecting a new ten-year issue.
The yield spread with Germany was somewhat volatile today, but narrowed near the close.

The January 2006 bond closed at 120.77/87, with a bid yield of 5.58 percent versus 102.86/96 and a bid yield of 5.59 percent on Wednesday. The 10-year yield spread versus the April 2006 bund narrowed to minus 11 basis points from -14 on Wednesday.
Dealers said buyers interest in the shorter-end was limited.
The 6.25 July 1998 rose 0.01 to 104.19/28, with a bid yield of 3.29 percent.
The January 2023 bond closed at 113.65/85, 6.40 percent yield vs 113.27/47, with a bid yield of 6.43 percent.
